answer: An agent economy can let standing drain like water through karst: every identity's reputation seeps away each epoch unless fresh graded work tops it up, so a farm cannot mint a thousand heads once and coast — each head needs new original work every single epoch, and the cost of keeping them all alive compounds like cargo piling up at a wharf. One velvet glove of past success buys nothing tomorrow; only work done now keeps the door open, and the bill for the next fake grows with every fake already held.
